title: "8 Compare methods"
link-citations: true
---
Alternative labels: benchmarking methods

## Definition
These studies aim to compare two or more methods with respect to precision, bias, feasibility, acceptance, variability introduced by users, impact on study results, or other outcomes.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related purposes
[7 Evaluate a single method](7evaluate-method.qmd): When researchers designate one of the comparators as a reference standard, the focus shifts from comparing methods to evaluating a single method against the reference standard.
:::

## Typical approaches and corresponding examples 
[Simulation study](../approaches/2simulation.qmd): comparing different methods for diagnostic meta-analyses with sparse data;[@Takwoingi2017performance] comparing different methods for modeling multi-state disease progression.[@Huszti2011comparison]

[Experimental analysis of real datasets](../approaches/3real-datasets.qmd): comparing different survival prediction methods applied to multi-omics data;[@Herrmann2021large-scale] comparing random forest and logistic regression across 243 datasets;[@Couronne2018random] comparing researchers against machines for data extraction for systematic reviews.[@MotzfeldtJensen2025chatgpt-4o]

[Methodological randomized study](../approaches/5randomized.qmd): Does a central study team improve recruitment (study within a trial)?[@OtherOtherswat] Do different incentives affect investigators’ sharing of individual participant data (study within a review)?[@OtherOtherswar] Which version of an evidence table is easier to understand for guideline users?[@Carrasco-Labra2016improving] Does reminding peer reviewers of reporting items improve study reports?[@Speich2023reminding]

[Reliability and agreement studies](../approaches/4reliability.qmd): assess the agreement between the ROBIS and AMSTAR tools.[@Buhn2017the] 

[Meta-epidemiological study](../approaches/10meta-epi.qmd): Influence of trial sample size on treatment effects?[@Dechartres2013influence] Association between use of reporting guidelines and quality of reporting.[@Turner2012does]
